title: TPMS component locations
introduction:
I read this drawing as a map of the tire pressure monitoring system's conversation. The wheel-mounted TPMS sensors transmit pressure information by radio to the RTM (radio transceiver module), which passes it to the BCM (body control module). The RTM is the receiving desk; the BCM coordinates TPMS operation. That helps explain why the system includes more than the little sensor tucked inside each wheel.

Match the circled callouts to the Item and Description table, then follow their leader lines to the highlighted locations. The sensor close-up shows its relationship to the wheel's valve area. The BCM leader points to the front footwell area. For the RTM, choose the entry matching the body style: the convertible location is beside the rear cabin area, while the coupe location is up near the rear roof area. Those are alternative body-style locations, rather than instructions to look for both modules in the same car. The table retains the required quantities.

Use this reference to identify the components and their general locations before choosing the relevant service information. TPMS can warn about low pressure or a system fault, but this map cannot determine which condition caused a warning. Pressure targets, diagnostic tests, sensor training and removal instructions belong to their respective procedures.
